title: Build a Promo Code System in JavaScript (Checkout Tutorial Part 3)
creator: Lena Fischer
description:
Part 3 of the checkout series: we add discount codes to the cart. Percentage codes, fixed-amount codes, expiry dates and one-use-per-customer.

Starter code is on my GitHub, link below.

Part 2: totals and tax

sentences.t: Hey everyone, welcome back to part three of the checkout series.
Last time we got the cart totals and tax working, and today we're adding discount codes.
This is honestly one of the most requested features, so let's get into it.
First, the data model.
I'm going to keep all our codes in a simple object for now, and later we'll move it into a database.
Each code has a type, which is either percent or fixed, an amount, an expiry date, and a flag for whether it can only be used once per customer.
So let me just type this out.
Okay, now let's write some test codes, so we have something to play with.
The first one is SAVE20, and that's a percentage code, so if a customer types in SAVE20 at checkout, they get twenty percent off the whole cart.
The second one is TENOFF, a fixed code, ten dollars off, but only if the order is over fifty dollars.
And the third one is WELCOME, which gives fifteen percent off your first order, and that's the one-use-per-customer code.
So in the UI, the customer pastes the code into this little box, hits apply, and the discount shows up right under the subtotal.
These codes aren't real, by the way, they don't work on any actual store, they're just test data for our app.
Now we need a function to actually apply the code.
I'm calling it applyDiscount, and it takes the cart and whatever string the user typed in.
The first thing we do is trim the input and make it uppercase.
Because people will absolutely type save twenty in lowercase with a space at the end, and we don't want that to fail.
Then we look the code up in our object.
If it doesn't exist, we return an error message, something friendly like, sorry, that code isn't valid.
If it does exist, we check the type.
For a percent code, we multiply the subtotal by the amount divided by a hundred.
For a fixed code, we just subtract the amount.
And here's a bug I see all the time in code reviews.
If the discount is bigger than the cart, you end up with a negative total, and then your store is paying the customer.
So we clamp it with Math dot max, zero, so the total can never go below zero.
Next, expiry.
Every code has an expiresAt date, so before we apply anything, we compare that to the current date.
If it's in the past, we return an error saying the code has expired.
One thing to watch out for here is time zones.
If your server is in a different time zone from your customer, a code might expire a few hours early or late.
For this tutorial I'm just using UTC everywhere, which is the sane default.
And then the one-use-per-customer rule.
For that, we keep a set of customer IDs that have already used the code.
If the current customer is in the set, we reject it.
If not, we apply the discount and add them to the set once the order actually goes through, not when they click apply.
Otherwise someone could apply it, abandon the cart, and lose the code forever.
Alright, let's test it.
I'll add a few items to the cart, a hoodie and two mugs.
Typing in the twenty percent code, hit apply, and there we go, the total drops.
Now let me try the ten dollar one on a small order.
And it says the order needs to be over fifty, perfect.
Let me try the welcome code twice with the same customer.
Second time, rejected, exactly what we want.
In part four we're going to hook this up to a real database and add an admin page where you can create codes without touching the code.
The starter files are linked below if you want to follow along.
See you in the next one.
